interface.name: labwc_control_v1

description.summary: control toplevels owned by other clients

interface.description:
This protocol allows privileged clients to set the absolute geometry of a toplevel owned by another client, to change its state, to activate it, and to ask it to close.
There is no standard protocol for the geometry part. The wlr- and ext-foreign-toplevel protocols expose a toplevel's state and allow requests to activate, close, maximize, minimize and fullscreen it, but not to move or resize it. Anything that needs to lay out windows itself - a tiler, a tiling script, a window switcher with previews, or an automation tool - has to rely on this or a private IPC mechanism instead.
The activate, close and set/unset requests do duplicate zwlr_foreign_toplevel_management_v1, but they are provided here as well because there is no way to correlate a zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 with an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1. Only the latter carries the stable identifier needed to tell two toplevels with the same title and app_id apart, so a client which has identified a toplevel by its identifier would otherwise have to guess which wlr handle belongs to it.
Toplevels are identified with the handles provided by ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1, so that a client can match what zcosmic-toplevel-info-v1 told it about geometry and state with what it is allowed to change here. The state requests cover exactly the states zcosmic-toplevel-info-v1 reports.

description.summary: destroy the labwc_control_v1 object

request.name: get_toplevel

description.summary: extend an existing foreign toplevel handle

request.description:
Request a labwc_control_toplevel_v1 for an existing ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.
The compositor may ignore all requests on the returned object if the toplevel is not currently managed by labwc, for example because it has already been closed.

request.name: cycle_next

description.summary: focus the next toplevel

request.description:
Moves keyboard focus to the next toplevel in the window switcher order, as if the user had pressed the NextWindow keybinding. Unlike the keybinding, this does not open the window switcher overlay.
This is not a request on a toplevel handle because it acts on whichever toplevel is active, not on a particular one.

request.name: cycle_prev

description.summary: focus the previous toplevel

request.description: Same as cycle_next, in the opposite direction.

interface.name: labwc_control_toplevel_v1

description.summary: set the geometry of a toplevel

interface.description:
All coordinates are in the compositor's global layout coordinate space, the same space wl_output.geometry reports output positions in.
Requests are applied immediately and are not acknowledged with an event. Clients wanting to know whether a request had the intended effect should watch the geometry event of the corresponding zcosmic_toplevel_handle_v1.
Because an absolute geometry is only meaningful for a floating view, the compositor takes the view out of any state that would otherwise override it (fullscreen, maximized, tiled, shaded) before applying the request.

description.summary: destroy the labwc_control_toplevel_v1 object

request.name: move_to

description.summary: move the toplevel to the given position

request.description: The position is the upper left corner of the window frame, including decorations.

request.name: resize_to

description.summary: resize the toplevel

request.description: The size is the size of the window frame, including decorations. The current position is kept.

request.name: move_resize_to

description.summary: move and resize the toplevel in one step

request.description: Equivalent to move_to followed by resize_to, but avoids an intermediate configure and the redraw that would go with it.

request.name: activate

description.summary: make the toplevel the active window

request.description:
Raises the toplevel and gives it keyboard focus, as if the user had clicked on it or picked it from a taskbar.
This duplicates a request of zwlr_foreign_toplevel_management_v1. It lives here because there is no way to correlate a zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 with the ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 this object was created from. Only the latter carries the stable identifier needed to tell two toplevels with the same title and app_id apart, so a client which has identified a toplevel by its identifier would otherwise have to guess which wlr handle belongs to it.

request.name: close

description.summary: ask the client to close the toplevel

request.description:
The client is free to ignore this, for example to ask the user to save unsaved changes first, so this does not guarantee that the toplevel goes away. Clients should watch for the closed event of the corresponding ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.
This duplicates a request of zwlr_foreign_toplevel_management_v1 for the same reason as activate.

request.name: set_maximized

description.summary: maximize the toplevel

request.description: Maximizes in both directions. Has no effect on a fullscreen toplevel.

request.name: unset_maximized

description.summary: restore the toplevel to its previous size

request.description: Restores the geometry the toplevel had before it was maximized.

request.name: set_minimized

description.summary: minimize the toplevel

request.description: Hides the toplevel without unmapping it. Any child toplevels are minimized as well.

request.name: unset_minimized

description.summary: restore a minimized toplevel

request.description: Shows the toplevel again and activates it.

request.name: set_fullscreen

description.summary: make the toplevel fullscreen

request.description: The toplevel goes fullscreen on the output it is currently on.

request.name: unset_fullscreen

description.summary: take the toplevel out of fullscreen

request.description: Restores the geometry the toplevel had before it went fullscreen.

request.name: set_sticky

description.summary: show the toplevel on all workspaces

request.description: This is the state zcosmic-toplevel-info-v1 calls sticky, and what labwc calls omnipresent.

description.summary: stop showing the toplevel on all workspaces

request.name: center

description.summary: center the toplevel on its output

request.description: Centers the toplevel in the usable area of the output it is on.

request.name: move_by

description.summary: move the toplevel relative to its position

request.description: A negative value moves left or up. Has no effect on a fullscreen toplevel.

request.name: resize_by

description.summary: resize the toplevel relative to its size

request.description:
Each argument is the amount by which to move the corresponding edge. Positive values grow the toplevel, negative values shrink it. A negative left or top value grows the toplevel towards the top left, which is what makes this more general than a plain width/height delta.
Has no effect on a fullscreen or maximized toplevel.

request.name: snap_to_edge

description.summary: move the toplevel against an edge of its output

request.description: Moves the toplevel as far as it can go in the given direction without leaving the usable area of its output.

arg.name: snap_to_windows
arg.summary: non-zero to stop at the edge of another toplevel

request.name: grow_to_edge

description.summary: grow the toplevel towards an edge of its output

request.description: Grows the toplevel by a maximum of 50%. Has no effect on a fullscreen or maximized toplevel.

request.name: shrink_to_edge

description.summary: shrink the toplevel away from an edge

request.description: The reverse of grow_to_edge. Has no effect on a fullscreen or maximized toplevel.

request.name: set_layer

description.summary: set the stacking layer of the toplevel

request.description: A toplevel is always in exactly one layer, so unlike the other state requests this one takes the new value rather than coming in a set and an unset variant.

request.name: set_shaded

description.summary: shade the toplevel

request.description: Rolls the toplevel up so that only its title bar is left. Has no effect on a toplevel without server side decorations.

description.summary: unshade the toplevel

request.name: set_decorations

description.summary: set the decorations of the toplevel

request.description: In the same way as the SetDecorations action, this is ignored when the toplevel requests decorations from the client and the requested mode would add to them.

description.summary: a direction to move or grow a toplevel in
stacking layer of a toplevel
how much of the decorations to draw
